stem: A client with post-traumatic stress disorder reports being easily startled, feeling constantly on guard, and having difficulty falling and staying asleep. Which PTSD symptom cluster do these findings represent?

options.A: Intrusion symptoms, which center on recurrent unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or intense reactions to trauma reminders.
options.B: Avoidance symptoms, which center on efforts to avoid trauma-related thoughts, feelings, people, places, or other reminders.
options.C: Arousal and reactivity symptoms, including exaggerated startle, feeling on guard or on edge, irritability, and sleep difficulty.
options.D: Negative cognition and mood symptoms, which include persistent negative beliefs, blame, emotional numbing, and loss of interest.

rationale: VA National Center for PTSD guidance places hypervigilance, heightened startle response, irritability and difficulty sleeping in Criterion E, alterations in arousal and reactivity. Option C matches the client's findings. Option A describes intrusion symptoms, option B describes avoidance, and option D describes negative alterations in cognitions and mood.
educational_objective: Recognize common PTSD arousal-and-reactivity symptoms and distinguish them from intrusion, avoidance, and negative cognition/mood symptoms.
source_version_date: DSM-5-TR published March 2022; adult PTSD criteria unchanged; VA guidance current as accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: DSM-5 Criteria for PTSD, Criterion E: trauma-related arousal and reactivity — hypervigilance, heightened startle reaction, difficulty concentrating, difficulty sleeping, irritability/aggression and risky/destructive behavior.
source_claim_supported: Hypervigilance, exaggerated startle and sleep difficulty belong to the PTSD alterations-in-arousal-and-reactivity cluster.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: p.10, Psychosocial Integrity — care and education for acute/chronic psychosocial health issues; appropriate care for clients with psychological/cognitive alterations.

source_original.stem: A client with post-traumatic stress disorder reports being easily startled, feeling constantly on guard, and having difficulty falling and staying asleep. Which PTSD symptom cluster do these findings represent?

options.A: Intrusion symptoms, which center on recurrent unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or intense reactions to trauma reminders.
options.B: Avoidance symptoms, which center on efforts to avoid trauma-related thoughts, feelings, people, places, or other reminders.
options.C: Arousal and reactivity symptoms, including exaggerated startle, feeling on guard or on edge, irritability, and sleep difficulty.
options.D: Negative cognition and mood symptoms, which include persistent negative beliefs, blame, emotional numbing, and loss of interest.

source_original.rationale: VA PTSD guidance places exaggerated startle, hypervigilance or feeling on guard, irritability, and sleep disturbance in the arousal-and-reactivity cluster. Option C is correct. Option A describes intrusion symptoms such as unwanted memories, nightmares, and flashbacks. Option B describes avoidance of trauma-related thoughts or reminders. Option D describes negative changes in beliefs, mood, interest, or connectedness rather than heightened arousal.
source_original.source_detail: VA National Center for PTSD — PTSD and DSM-5, Criterion E: Alterations in arousal and reactivity; includes hypervigilance/being on guard, exaggerated startle response, concentration problems, and sleep disturbance. VA notes DSM-5-TR did not change adult PTSD diagnostic criteria. Current VA National Center for PTSD professional guidance; DSM-5-TR adult PTSD criteria current; live source rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: mental-health symptom recognition, therapeutic communication, behavioral adaptation and culturally/person-centered psychosocial support as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the original stem, answer key and construct. Reverified VA Criterion E and tightened the rationale/locator to the current VA description without adding diagnostic claims beyond the symptom cluster.

audit_findings.source_authority: VA National Center for PTSD professional guidance summarizing DSM-5/DSM-5-TR adult PTSD criteria.
audit_findings.currentness: VA page rechecked 2026-08-16; page states DSM-5-TR made no changes to adult PTSD diagnostic criteria.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Criterion E directly lists hypervigilance, heightened startle reaction and difficulty sleeping.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Stem asks only for symptom-cluster classification and does not infer severity, duration or a new diagnosis.

distractor_audit.A: Intrusion cluster contains memories/nightmares/flashbacks, not the presented findings.
distractor_audit.D: Negative cognition/mood involves negative beliefs, blame, reduced interest or detachment.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The three presented findings all map to Criterion E; no competing cluster contains this combination.
audit_findings.cueing: All options name legitimate PTSD symptom clusters with concise examples.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN 2026 p.10 Psychosocial Integrity covers psychosocial health issues and care for psychological/cognitive alterations.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial reread confirmed C remains uniquely best and each distractor describes a different DSM-5 PTSD cluster.
